# Front Endpaper

->**[Decorative Marbled Endpaper]**<-

->This page features a classic example of <term>marbled paper<note>A decorative paper produced by floating pigments on a liquid bath and "combing" or swirling them into patterns before laying paper on top to transfer the design.</note></term>. This specific design is known as a "snail" or "shell" pattern, characterized by the tight, rhythmic spirals that resemble a mollusk's shell. The palette consists of vibrant orange, charcoal grey, and soft yellow on an off-white base. Marbled endpapers were commonly used in high-quality bookbinding to hide the raw edges of the leather where it was folded over the boards and to provide a visually striking entrance to the text.<-

# SUMMARY OF THE INDIVIDUAL BOOKS
->*of this Treatise.*<-

**BOOK 1** Concerning the Egyptian Hieroglyphic <note>In Maier's time, before the discovery of the Rosetta Stone, hieroglyphs were believed to be purely symbolic or mystical icons representing hidden philosophical truths.</note> Deities: Osiris, Isis, Mercury, Vulcan, Typhon, etc.; and concerning the marvelous works of the Kings, the characters of individual living creatures, and other monuments pertaining to this subject.

**BOOK 2** Concerning the allegories of the Greeks, especially the "golden" ones, such as the Golden Fleece of Jason, the Golden Apples of the Hesperides, etc., which denote nothing other than the golden medicine <note>The "golden medicine" refers to the Philosopher's Stone or the Universal Panacea, which alchemists believed could cure all diseases and transmute base metals into gold.</note>.

**BOOK 3** Concerning the golden fictitious genealogy of the gods and goddesses, whether Philosophical or Chemico-medical <note>original: "Chymico-medica." This refers to iatrochemistry, the school of thought that used chemical treatments rather than just herbal ones to cure illness.</note>.

**BOOK 4** Concerning the festivals and sacred rites, as well as the contests and games, established for the sake of this science <note>Maier argues that ancient religious festivals were actually public commemorations of secret alchemical processes.</note>.

**BOOK 5** Concerning the Labors of Hercules, which signify the same craftsmanship <term>artificium</term> <note>The "Artificium" or "Great Work" is the step-by-step process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>.

I **BOOK 6** Concerning the Trojan expedition and the requirements without which Troy could not be captured, and the wanderings of Ulysses, pertaining to the same <note>original: "Ulyssis." Maier interprets the Odyssey and the Iliad as massive alchemical allegories.</note>.

->distinguishing him from the *Mocker* and the *Buffoon*<-
<note>In classical tradition, *Momus* was the god of mockery and unfair criticism, while a *Mime* (*Mimus*) represented a superficial actor or buffoon. Maier uses these figures to contrast the serious, fair-minded reader with those who would dismiss or misunderstand his alchemical secrets.</note>

The <term>Daughter of SATURN<gloss>Truth (Veritas)</gloss></term> is rescued from the shadows by our toil,

And brought forth anew into the light, she is offered through labor;
Reader, see, O honest one, she is carried into your arms,

Nothing is easier for the *Mockers* than to despise even the best of works,

But nothing is more difficult than to produce things that might please the *Buffoons*.

# MICHAEL MA-
## IER, IMPERIAL COUNT PALATINE,
### PREFACE TO THE READERS.

**I**f you wonder, kind readers, what cause arose for me, why I should publish this treatise distinguished by the name **OF THE MOST SECRET THINGS** <note>original: "ARCANISSIMORVM"</note> after so many and such great authors published on the subjects of Hieroglyphics, allegories, fables, theology, philosophy, poetry, *Chemistry* <note>original: "Chymicis". In the 17th century, the term "Chymistry" encompassed both practical laboratory work and the symbolic, spiritual pursuit of alchemy.</note> and medicine—and why I have finally scattered it into the public light of the world, and specifically addressed it to you to be judged despite so many existing prejudices—once you have looked upon the matter itself, my studies and intentions, and your own integrity all at once, you will without doubt cease to wonder.

Among Christians, I believe, there is no one so unskilled in all things—provided they possess common sense and hold the first rudiments of literature—who has not at some time read the books of the *Pagans* <note>original: "Ethnicorum", referring to non-Christian classical authors like the Greeks and Romans.</note> (of which a vast number has reached our age) and has not observed these two things within them: First, the names of gods, goddesses, and heroes, such as *Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Apollo, Juno, Venus, Pallas, Hercules, Jason*, and the rest; Second, the monstrous, horrendous, and incredible deeds of each of these gods and heroes. For all the books of the *Pagans* are so stuffed with these two things that on almost every single page, by hammering them in, they contain hardly anything else worthy of memory. 

*For example*, if one were to take away the gods and the deeds of the gods and the heroes descended from gods from *Homer* and *Herodotus* among the *Greeks*, or from *Livy* and *Virgil* among the *Romans*, the greatest part of their works would be marked with an <term>obelisk<gloss>a critical mark (—) used by ancient grammarians and editors to indicate that a passage of text is suspicious, spurious, or should be deleted</gloss></term>. For the deeds are so bound together with the persons, and the persons with the deeds, that if one is removed, the other cannot stand.

<summary>Michael Maier introduces his work on "The Most Secret Things," arguing that classical Greek and Roman literature is fundamentally inseparable from the "monstrous" myths of gods and heroes.</summary>
<keywords>Michael Maier, alchemy, classical mythology, Greek literature, Roman literature, Arcanissima, gods and heroes</keywords>

# Preface

or if one is granted, let the other also be granted: the same judgment will apply to the rest of the **Pagan** authors and their writings. But we Christians have long ago cast aside, mocked, and ridiculed that multitude of gods, as we are instructed by the truth of the Word of God: What then shall we say of the deeds of so many gods and heroes? Are these things possible and true, even though the ones who supposedly performed them were not gods and were false? Or shall we indeed refute and reject the gods, yet nonetheless admit and receive their deeds and their progeny? Shall we pronounce these stories to be as false as the gods themselves, and conclude there is no truth in either among any of these authors? 

It is a wonder that no one among so many myriads of writing Christians has been concerned about this, when the explanation of these difficulties is so necessary that hardly any writing, whether political or **Theosophical** <note>original: "Theosophicum". Referring to "divine wisdom" or the study of God through nature and mystical insight.</note> after the sacred scriptures, could be offered to the world more usefully. But the reason for this neglect is that these matters seem not only most ancient and stored beyond all memory of writers, but also most secret—insofar as they have always been kept from their true origin and have remained known to very few. 

For those things ought by right to be deemed most ancient and at the same time **MOST SECRET** which, through so many ages of the world—for more than three thousand years, from the first authors even to our own times—have been covered and hidden like a **Treasure** <note>original: "Thesaurus"</note> enclosed most securely in a chest. Although **Pagan** writers have unrolled some of these things (albeit fabulous things in a fabulous manner—that is, according to their own limited understanding), they called them "mysteries." This is clear from the titles of the books of **Eumolpus, Menander, Melanthius, Iamblichus, Evanthis**, and others <note>Maier lists various ancient Greek and Neoplatonist authors associated with the "Mysteries" of Eleusis or esoteric philosophy.</note> who contain nothing besides poetic fables and do not truly explain even a jot of them. They wrote in this way because they understood that great and mystical things lie hidden under these fictions, containing in reality more in their depths than they promise on the surface. 

For the ancient **Egyptians**, the wisest of men (from whom, if we seek the first origin, we will notice all these things have been propagated), when they had obtained most precious things by the gift of **GOD** and their own labor, which they did not want to be entirely unknown to posterity, nor yet equally known to everyone, found a way of obscuring them, and as if wrapping them in certain darkness, so that

<summary>Maier argues that while Christians reject Pagan gods, the myths themselves contain hidden "most secret" truths—originally devised by wise Egyptians—that have remained unexplained for three thousand years.</summary>
<keywords>Egyptian wisdom, Pagan mythology, Christian interpretation, Michael Maier, ancient mysteries, Theosophy, hidden truth</keywords>

# To the Readers

...unless endowed with the sharpest light of the mind, they might suspect anything of them; and thus they devised ***hieroglyphic letters, allegories, and fables***, in which, as if in cloisters and prisons, they contained and hid matters not to be made public for as long as they pleased, so that those seeing and hearing would not immediately understand, but would at least have reason to inquire. Truly, how much evil has arisen from this can scarcely be said or believed: For just as we read that in **Babylonia**, in the temple of **Apollo**, a golden casket of wonderful antiquity was once discovered, from which, when it was broken and opened, such a force of pestilential and most destructive air poured forth, that its blast not only finished off those who were present, infected by a poisonous and lethal stain, but spreading with pestilential and incredible power, it even afflicted the **Parthians** far and wide; Or as in the times of **Marcus Antonius** <note>Maier likely refers to the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus</note> and **Verus** at **Seleucia**, when certain soldiers opened a narrow hole—which the priests <note>original: "vates"</note> of the **Chaldeans** <note>An ancient people of Mesopotamia famous for astronomy and occult wisdom.</note> had previously closed—after the temple of **Apollo** had been plundered and his image moved to **Rome**, such a fatal and foul vapor emerged that it raged violently from the borders of the **Persians** through **Syria**, all of **Greece**, and its neighboring regions even to **Gaul** (**as Ammianus Marcellinus and from him Caelius Rhodiginus <note>Ludovico Ricchieri, a Renaissance scholar known by his Latin name Calvisius Rhodiginus.</note> in book 5, chapter 12, recount,**) so it happened with the treasures of the **Egyptians** hidden under their secret coverings, that when opened otherwise than was proper, they filled all **Greece**, and after it the whole world, with superstitions, a multitude of most vain gods, and astonishing deeds: This evil lasted throughout the entire time of **Paganism**, until the true Physician of the soul, our **SAVIOR**, arrived, who provided for the human race with a far different remedy than **Hippocrates** (who rendered the **Athenians** immune from that plague by burning forests) and utterly ruined and destroyed those idols of the nations, namely by the most secret, saving **WORD** brought forth from the bosom of the **ETERNAL FATHER**: Since then, the gods of the nations in the Church and the Christian world have long been cheapened and rejected as fictitious and vain. But since nevertheless, as has been said, so many monuments and books of the **Pagans** <note>original: "Ethnicorum"</note> are published daily...

<summary>Maier compares the "opening" of secret Egyptian knowledge to the release of a plague from an ancient casket, arguing that misunderstood allegories led to the spread of pagan idolatry until the arrival of Christ. He uses the historical account of the plague under Marcus Aurelius as a metaphor for how misinterpreted secrets can infect the world.</summary>

<keywords>Hieroglyphs, allegories, Seleucia, Apollo, plague of Marcus Aurelius, Ammianus Marcellinus, Hippocrates, Paganism, Word of God, Egyptian secrets</keywords>

# Preface

...so that they are held in the hands of the learned, in almost every paragraph of which mention is made of the **gods and heroes of the nations**; this gave the cause to the erudite to diligently investigate what exactly was understood by those gods and heroes. Therefore, some were found who reduced them to **history** <note>This approach is known as Euhemerism, the theory that gods were originally historical kings or heroes.</note>, as if those gods and heroes were kings and men in ancient ages, and performed such great and numerous things as are written of them; others applied them to the formation of morals or to the natural reasoning of this world.

But since these people frequently produced things most absurd—worthy neither of those first, wisest men to wrap up, nor of themselves to unwrap—and for the most part corrupted them with their own fictions produced without any agreement of reality, they left more doubt than certainty in the minds of readers. Many have therefore wished that what truly lay beneath those gods and heroes of the nations might finally be thoroughly expressed. For it is certainly credible that it was not some trivial thing, arising from history, nor to be drawn toward morals or other matters, that existed at the start; a thing which involved nearly the whole world and so many wise men in it, not for a mere hundred years (which would be too much), but for thirty times a hundred or more—that is, **three thousand years**—and held them involved and blinded.

Meanwhile, among those who treat of **chemical matters**, some have come forward who assert that the pagan gods and goddesses took their first origin from chemical works. Among these were **Braceschus** <note>Giovanni Bracesco (c. 1481–1555), an Italian alchemist who wrote dialogues interpreting Geber and Aristotle.</note>, **Robertus Vallensis** <note>Robert Duval (c. 1490–1567), author of the first history of alchemy.</note>, and several others. But since they partly accommodated individual things to their own private concerns, and did not sufficiently render the reasoning and harmony of all things in a convenient method, and partly because **chemistry** itself is held by the judgment of many to be vain, futile, and useless, hence nothing certain could be judged by the learned concerning these matters.

Therefore, I have finally taken this labor upon myself, led by various causes: namely, to declare and set before the eyes of readers in one treatise what things were originally understood under the **gods, goddesses, and heroes of the nations**, and by what reasoning those fables have been propagated until now through the ages of the world. This is done both so that the truth of **Christian doctrine**, shining sufficiently by itself, may be more and more illustrated once these shadows are removed, and so that **Chemistry**—not **Alchemy** <term>Alcumia: Maier uses this term pejoratively here to distinguish "puffers" and fraudulent "gold-makers" from the true philosophical art of "Chymia."</term> (that nurse of so many rascals and mother of deceptions, which adulterates metals and does not truly transmute them), but that which serves to produce the **Golden Medicine**, the **Most Ancient** and **Most True**, may be demonstrated...

<meta>The text ends mid-word with "demon-", continuing on the next page with the catchword "stretur" to form "demonstretur" (may be demonstrated).</meta>

<summary>Michael Maier argues that ancient Greek and Roman myths are actually encoded chemical secrets, criticizing historical or moral interpretations in favor of a "Golden Medicine." He distinguishes true chemical science from fraudulent alchemy, promising to reveal the original meaning of the pagan gods.</summary>

<keywords>mythology, alchemy, Golden Medicine, Braceschus, Robertus Vallensis, chemical philosophy, Euhemerism, Christian doctrine</keywords>

## To the Readers.

*...so that it may stand, and this **SO GREAT A GIFT OF GOD** may be vindicated from the blasphemies of detractors. No one, I think, will judge gold—the finest metal, which has been accepted according to the value of things in the world as long as the world has existed and will exist, and which is usually applied to curing many human diseases—as something useless, most harmful, and detestable. Nor will he proscribe and accuse it because he does not have as large a supply of it as he would wish, nor because it does not remove all the afflictions, diseases, and desires of men, or because it is the alluring cause of many evils: theft, robbery, murder, adultery, and almost all vices being committed; unless he wishes to live entirely outside the world and appear as a Cynic <note>The Cynics were an ancient school of philosophy that advocated living in accordance with nature and rejecting worldly goods. The name "Cynic" derives from the Greek word for "dog."</note>. Let the same judgment apply to Medicine: If, therefore, medicine comes from gold, or gold from this medicine, who but the most insane would detest that medicine? He is a child in the world who thinks everything is the same everywhere as it is in his own home, or city, or region where he was raised. He is twice a child who, being of age, thinks there have never been nor are any who have seen, known, and understood more in these matters than he himself can grasp. Therefore, no one of sound judgment will deny the truth of Chemistry <term>Chymia: In this period, the term "chemistry" encompassed both what we now call chemistry and alchemy, focusing on the transmutation of metals and the creation of medicines.</term> because he does not see, know, or understand it. For this would be a mark of the most impudent mind: to accept only those beings known to himself and wish to banish the unknown from the universe of things. This would be, I say, an envious and dog-like <note>original: "canini". This is a pun on the Cynic philosophers mentioned earlier, suggesting a snarling, unreasoning hostility.</note> habit, not a human one: to deprive the world of that which he himself does not use. But lest anyone should imagine that, in bringing forth such a writing, I profess a mastery of this same matter, let them understand the nature of my studies: Having professed Galenic medicine <term>Galenic medicine: The traditional medical system based on the works of the Greek physician Galen, which focused on balancing the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile).</term> up to this point, I have not ceased to investigate other things, if there were any most secret matters within Chemistry. For I judged this to be characteristic of a liberally educated man, since just as birds seem born for flying, so he is born for reasoning. We see that not just one part of the air is open to birds, but the whole universe; why should it not be the same for men in their reasoning? Hence, let no one be angry with me if, beyond common knowledge, I desire to know even secret and rare things, having their foundation in the natures of things, proven by reason and experience, and most true. For Aristotle demonstrates in his *Metaphysics* <note>Referring to the opening line of Aristotle's Metaphysics: "All men by nature desire to know."</note> that this is proper to the intelligent soul. Indeed, moved by that passion, I have also visited foreign places, and thus also into this most celebrated kingdom...*

# Preface

I arrived at a point where, while I was more intensely focused on advancing my studies, this offspring was born under my pen. It is not a mere servant, but a forerunner of that Medicine which I have sought until now. It is not so immature that it cannot live, as some might imagine; for I have nurtured it within me longer than they say elephants carry their young in the womb. Yet I must confess, I have sent it out into the light through a "bear-like birth" <note>original: *ursino partu*. This refers to an ancient belief that bear cubs were born as formless lumps and had to be licked into shape by their mothers; Maier is suggesting his work is still in a somewhat unpolished state.</note> and "crude wisdom" <note>original: *rudis Minerva*, a Latin idiom for a work that is unrefined or lacks formal polish.</note>. For I was not as concerned with words as I was with things, nor was I seeking to capture some small glory for myself so much as I was concerned with providing a benefit to others.

Accept, therefore, kind readers, this labor of mine—whatever its quality may be—which is new in this genre. Just as it will not seem unnecessary to true Theology, so it will be most useful to the entire Circle of Learning <term>Ency-clopadiæ: From the Greek "enkyklios paideia," meaning the "circle of arts and sciences" that constitutes a complete education.</term>—including Politics and Civil Life (which Jurisprudence treats), Medicine, Chemistry, Poetry, History, Astronomy, Physics, and the other sciences and arts. 

And although this work may seem to contain paradoxes, in that it breaks with what has been accepted for so many centuries, I believe that whatever agrees with the truth in all things should be embraced, even if it disagrees with the opinions of the greater part of the world. Since we follow this principle in divine matters, why should we not also follow it in those human matters which are judged to come closest to them (as these do)? 

But if anyone prefers to approve of Paganism and the multitude of gods, and chooses not to recognize Chemistry—which is true even if unknown to him—in these myths, pleasing himself with some sharp critical wit, let him do as he pleases. Meanwhile, he will never make the falsehood of those opinions seem true to the wise, nor will he make the truth of this art seem vain. 

You, who carry a spark of Promethean light in your breast, who carry the wisdom of Pallas Athena in your soul—even if you do not recognize a common altar with those critics at the hearth of Vulcan or Vesta <note>Vulcan and Vesta represent the alchemical fire and the domestic hearth; Maier is addressing those who understand the "fire" of the laboratory.</note>—should protect this study of ours from the injuries of the envious and the "scourgers" <note>original: *mastygum*, referring to harsh, whip-wielding critics.</note> according to your own integrity. You should see to it that Truth is dug up and dragged out of the deep well or cave (into which Democritus testified it was immersed with laughter, and Heraclitus with tears) with all your might. 

To you alone, I say, who have been granted a heart to be wise above others, these 

->**MOST SECRET SECRETS**<- 

are opened and revealed, as you are the ones who know how to cast your vote <note>original: *calculum ferre*, referring to the ancient practice of voting with stones.</note> on these matters with a genuine dexterity of judgment. To the rest, however—the commoners, the unlearned, and those inexperienced in these matters—

<summary>Maier introduces his work as a "bear-like birth" (unpolished but vital) that interprets ancient myths as alchemical secrets. He argues that this knowledge is useful across all disciplines, from theology to physics, and appeals to "wise" readers to help him rescue Truth from its hidden well.</summary>

## BOOK ONE.
# ON THE HIERO-
# GLYPHICS OF THE EGYPTIANS.

<margin>Where the first humans were.</margin>
**T**hose who have compiled the history of the most ancient Egyptian affairs—or rather, their fabulous deeds—have handed down nothing certain regarding the origin of the first letters or sciences. Likewise, they provide no certainty concerning the first kings in the world (who were believed to be gods) or the birth of the first men. Instead, whatever they have written about these matters is very much like the mere fictions of idle men, the delusions of the melancholic, or the fantasies of dreamers. Some assert that the first humans were produced in Egypt, based on the conjecture that around the Thebaid <note>A region in Upper Egypt centered around the city of Thebes, often associated in antiquity with the origins of civilization.</note>, when the flooding of the Nile <note>The seasonal flooding of the Nile was essential for Egyptian agriculture, depositing nutrient-rich silt.</note> ceased and the sun warmed the mud left behind by the water, a multitude of mice arose from the cracks in the earth in many places. They suggest that, just as in the very beginning of the world, all living creatures and even humans themselves were born in a similar fashion. But Diodorus Siculus <note>A Greek historian from the 1st century BCE; his "Library of History" is a primary source for ancient myths and geography.</note>, who traveled through the greater part of Asia and Europe, as well as Egypt (as he himself admits), 
<margin>The first Kings.
Book 1, chapter 1.</margin>
says: "Regarding who the first kings in the world were, we have found no certainty at all, since no historians provide evidence to the contrary. Indeed, it is impossible for writing to have existed as early as the first kings. If, however, anyone should contend that letters existed even then, certainly those who wrote of such things 
<margin>The first letters and writers.</margin>
lived much later." Not only do the Greeks and other writers doubt what that more ancient age produced, but even those who call themselves the Indigetes <note>A term for the "original" or "earth-born" inhabitants of a land; in Roman mythology, these were local deities or ancestors.</note> and the first to [witness] events...

### Hieroglyphics, Book 1.

...barbarian writers call these things the necessities of life.

<margin>Book 1, chapter 2. The First Gods.</margin>
The same author <note>Diodorus Siculus, the Greek historian mentioned on the previous page.</note>, in the very next chapter, relates that the Sun and Moon were worshipped as eternal Gods by the first men, and that the former was called *Osiris* while the latter was called *Isis*, for specific linguistic reasons. However, just as we have accepted from the Holy Bible—as an indubitable truth—who the one and true God of Gods is, and when and where the first men and kings of the world appeared; so too do we recognize the vanity of the *Egyptians* in this matter, as well as in their claims of antiquity and a numbered series of kings continuing for more than twenty thousand years. Since they say elsewhere that *Isis* and *Osiris* were born of *Saturn* <note>Maier points out a logical contradiction: the Egyptians claim these gods are "eternal," yet also give them a father (Saturn/Kronos), implying a beginning.</note>, it is a wonder why they consider them the first eternal and unbegotten gods, or celestial lights. We can, however, excuse the Pagan writers if they handed down things differently than they truly are, both because their true nature could not be known due to their extreme antiquity (since the sacred history of *Moses* was unknown to them), and because the accepted religion of the Gods at that time did not allow them to think otherwise. 

<margin>The proposition and summary of the entire treatise.</margin>
As for us, to establish the foundation of *Egyptian* doctrine, we have determined through innumerable signs that a certain science existed in Egypt that teaches the most secret works of nature. This was the **GOLDEN MEDICINE**—not made *from* gold, but a thousand times more precious than gold—which was in use especially among the most ancient Philosophers, Priests, and Kings. In order that this science might be passed down to wiser posterity while remaining unknown to the common crowd, they commonly employed hidden marks taken from animals (later called <term>Hieroglyphics</term> <note>From the Greek *hieros* (sacred) and *glypho* (to carve).</note> by the Greeks) for their writing. For the explanation of these things, they frequently used Allegories drawn from fictional persons and their deeds. Hence, in succeeding times, as the minds of ignorant men became preoccupied with superstition, those fictional persons were regarded as Gods or kings, and the animals were worshipped as sacred and inviolable; one finds that eternal monuments were established for each of them.

Concerning the Gods of the Egyptians</margin> hieroglyphic Sun, Moon, Fire, air, water, and earth, and the rest of the wandering stars—gave the art's components names derived from them. For in the Subject of the art, two things are considered, of which one possesses the nature of the male and the other the nature of the female; therefore, they called the former *Osiris* or the *Sun*, and the latter *Isis* or the *Moon*. *Mercury*, who is joined to the *Sun* and *Moon*, is common to both, since no conjunction of the *Sun* and *Moon* occurs in the greater world unless *Mercury* is also present, for he always runs alongside as a satellite to the *Sun*. And just as these two are spouses, so too are they held to be brother and sister, to whom a certain third red and burning spirit is joined, called *Typhon*, who cuts his brother of the same womb, *Osiris*, into the smallest parts and limbs <note>This refers to the alchemical process of dissolution or "chemical death," allegorized by the myth of Typhon/Set dismembering Osiris.</note>. To these they add *Vulcan*, or external fire; *Pallas* <note>Athena</note>, or the wisdom of working; *Oceanus*, the generator of the gods, or the mother *Thetis*, or for both of them the *Nile* (that is, water); and the earth, the mother of all, who as *Orpheus* says, bestows riches; then *Saturn*, *Jupiter*, *Venus*, *Apollo*, *Pluto*, and other *Gods*. <margin>What Osiris represents.</margin>
*Osiris*, as has been stated, is understood without any evasion to be the material of the art <note>The "material of the art" refers to the "Prime Matter," the raw substance alchemists believed was necessary to begin their work.</note> from which the <term>Golden Medicine</term> <note>Another name for the Philosopher's Stone, believed to cure all diseases and transmute metals.</note> is composed. <margin>What Isis represents.</margin>
these pieces are collected and united by *Isis* after the completion of the work, once the combustible sulfur has been separated. Thus, the collection of the parts of *Osiris* undertaken by *Isis* is the "reiteration" <note>In alchemy, "reiteration" refers to repeating a process like distillation or sublimation to increase the purity and power of a substance.</note> of the same work. This continues until the power of *Typhon* is extinguished, and in its place, the Soul of *Osiris* succeeds, becoming sufficiently "burning" <note>original: "ardens"; implying a state of high energetic or spiritual activity in the chemical matter.</note> so that he easily converts his mother *Isis* (who is also his most loving wife and sister) to himself. This is the ultimate perfection of the work.

<margin>What Typhon represents.</margin>
We have already said what *Typhon* is: namely, a fiery and furious spirit <note>Typhon represents the "volatile" or corrosive aspect of the chemicals that "attacks" and breaks down the solid matter (Osiris).</note> that quickly penetrates our *Osiris* and snatches him into his own color, like a poison. This should occur not in the first, but in the final "cooking" or decoction. For the fire kindled in the vessel must not be made too sharp by <term>Vulcan</term> <note>Vulcan was the Roman god of fire; here it refers to the heat of the furnace.</note> at the beginning; otherwise, like the fire of Hell, it will burn the entire body of *Osiris* so that he can never be restored to life by his mother.

<margin>Note.</margin>
It must be noted here that *Isis* and *Osiris* are one and the same subject <note>In alchemical theory, many seemingly different ingredients are actually different states or "faces" of a single underlying substance.</note>, containing within it both the male *Osiris* and the female *Isis*. It is also both *Osiris* the son and *Isis* the mother; or *Osiris* the brother and *Isis* the sister. Thus, it behaves like a <term>Hermaphrodite</term> or <term>Androgyne</term>, being used and accepted now as *Osiris* and now as *Isis* because it reflects both sexes. It is named differently according to the relationship—husband and wife, brother and sister, or mother and son. Since this subject is unique in the nature of things, and specific to **Alchemy**, it is known to the craftsmen; to them, *Osiris* and *Isis* will become known along with their entire family and the sequence of their deeds. The fact that the Egyptian Priests possess an image of *Osiris*, claim to be the only ones who know the location of his tomb, and assert that it is in their keeping without revealing it to anyone, shows nothing else than this: they admit, albeit through Allegory, that they are skilled in and possess the **Alchemical** art, yet they are willing to reveal it to no one except the most worthy.

It appears, moreover, that this last of the gods reigned after his father *Osiris* was translated to the gods. They say that *Horus* is interpreted as *Apollo* <note>In alchemical symbolism, Apollo represents the Sun or gold.</note>, and having been taught the art of healing and divination by his mother *Isis*, he brought much benefit to humanity through both oracles and medicines.

Here it must be observed that *Osiris* was previously called the brother of *Apollo* and *Isis*, since all these are said to be born of *Jove* and *Juno*; yet now *Apollo* is called the son of *Isis* and *Osiris*. This reversal of roles occurs only within true **Alchemy** <note>original: "Chymia"</note>. For since the active and passive principles are so homogeneous and of a single kind, the same thing can be father, mother, son, daughter, grandfather, grandmother, grandson, granddaughter, brother, sister, husband, and wife, and other similar relations. This is a source of wonder and is unique to this Art.

It is believable that *Isis* provides medicines to humanity; for how much power that substance called *Isis* possesses in medicine has long since been known to the world. It is established as a most certain truth that her son *Horus*, or *Apollo*, is the last of the Egyptian gods. For he is the very one for whom his mother and father, grandfather and great-grandfathers undertook so many labors, migrated to the Indies and other parts of the world, and performed so many stupendous works.

He is the treasure, the love, and the care of the Egyptian Philosophers, Priests, and Kings, for whose sake they honor his parents, hold them in delight, and celebrate them solemnly. This is that **philosophical offspring** born of *Isis* and *Osiris*—or, if you prefer, *Apollo* born of *Jove* and *Latona*—concerning whose birth, as well as that of his sister the Moon or *Cynthia*, we shall speak below. 

The rejoicing philosophers have mentioned him in many places: namely, that he is born from the **Red Servant** <note>original: "Seruo rubeo"; an alchemical term for a specific stage or reagent in the process</note>, also known as the father *Gabritius*, and the mother *Beya* <note>Gabritius and Beya are classic alchemical allegories for the Solar/Sulfuric and Lunar/Mercurial principles whose "marriage" produces the Stone.</note>. He is destined to be far more noble than his parents. Furthermore, the son must be joined again in marriage with the mother; that is, the **cooked** must be joined with the **raw** and cooked again <note>This refers to the alchemical process of "reiteration" or "circulation," where the refined product is fed back into the starting material to increase its potency.</note>, until one inseparable, homogeneous thing is made from the two: namely, the perfect spirit. *Isaac* <note>likely Isaac Hollandus, a famous alchemical writer</note> in book 2, chapter 26, says that *Morienus* <note>Morienus Romanus, a legendary hermit-alchemist</note> speaks of this: "Make the conjunction and grant him a soul from it, so that he may never be separated from that soul for eternity: Make..."

### Hieroglyphics Book 1.

And the Priests had sons who were Priests, just as individual craftsmen have sons who are craftsmen; nor was it permitted for anyone else to aspire to the priesthood, but it was a matter of necessity for each to take up his father’s duty or trade. 

By this reasoning, it did not become known to other inhabitants, besides the Priests, that this knowledge existed in the world; much less to foreigners, who for the same reason were strictly barred from Egypt, or if they had arrived, were driven back with shame or at the risk of their lives. When, however, the neighboring Greek people arrived later, enticed by the benevolence of a certain King and stirred by a certain obscure rumor, it is established that the most secret Egyptian arts were also propagated to other parts of the world, as we shall discuss more broadly later.

### Book 1 of the Egyptian-Greeks.

...if he had been exhausted, he would without a doubt have been forced to reveal the entire art to **Alexander the Great**, who then possessed **Egypt**. Thus, under the fabulous coverings of **Osiris** and **Isis**, they concealed the art for as long as they wished. For if it had been publicly established that **Osiris** and **Isis** were neither gods nor humans—and likewise that **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, **Mars**, **Mercury**, **Apollo**, **Diana**, **Venus**, and **Vulcan** had never lived or reigned—and yet so many great sacrifices were made and honors shown to each of them, it would have provided an opportunity for the curious to investigate what exactly was contained and hidden under those veiled names. This seemed entirely contrary to reason to the Egyptian Priests and was associated with the greatest danger; and therefore they were compelled to assert that such figures were not gods, but men who had been received into the order of the gods. And so they gave **Alexander** a reason—since the gods of the major nations, so celebrated by divine worship throughout the world, had at least been men and kings—to allow himself also to be worshipped and proclaimed as a God, even though he was confined within a mortal body. 

Besides the worship of **Osiris** and **Isis**, it is known from histories among the Egyptians that honors were also given to **Hercules**, and that the *Eleusinia* <note>The Eleusinian Mysteries, usually associated with Greece, are here claimed to have Egyptian origins.</note> or the most secret rites of **Ceres** were established, as well as those for other Gods, namely **Vulcan**, **Mercury**, **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and the like; but leaving those to be unfolded elsewhere, we shall now turn ourselves to the more famous kings of the Egyptians.

This city, built as a miracle of art and nature and endowed by individual Philosopher-Kings with so many stupendous and most precious works, is observed to be consecrated in honor of **Orus** <note>Horus.</note>, or Apollo, or the Sun—not the celestial star, but the *Philosophical Sun*, produced from the earth and elaborated by the work of Vulcan <note>The god of fire; in alchemy, this refers to the controlled heat of the furnace used to "perfect" metals into gold.</note>, the last of the gods. No foreigner was permitted to see or enter this city, although its fame was spread far and wide through the world. Hence, the Greeks writing about it pronounced nothing certain, as they were not eyewitnesses, but scattered dreams and incredible tales of "Hundred-Gated Egyptian Thebes" everywhere. This city alone, built for luxury and the display of wealth, could provide sufficient and most evident proof of the Egyptians' <term>chemical Artifice</term> <note>original: "chymico Artificio"; refers to the alchemical skill of transmuting base metals into gold.</note> to those who consider the matter more acutely. ...one part of the wall contained a carved depiction of a city under siege, situated by a part where a river washed against the walls. There, the King was shown joined in battle with a portion of the enemy, and a **Lion** joined the fight alongside him, turning the enemy to flight. Some writers report this to be a true history, saying that the king was accustomed to using the assistance of a lion raised in his own home to achieve victory in battle. Others claim that because of the King's exceptional physical bravery, he wished to display the strength of his body and spirit through the likeness of a lion.

...where the body of the king was seen to be buried. Surrounding the monuments was a **golden circle**, 365 cubits <note>Approximately 547 feet or 167 meters.</note> in circumference and one cubit thick. On this circle, each cubit was marked with a day of the year and the rising and setting of the stars, along with what those observations signified according to the Egyptian astrologers. They say this circle was <margin>Note.</margin> carried away during the time when **Cambyses** <note>The Persian King who conquered Egypt in 525 BCE.</note> and the Persians ruled the Egyptians. 

These most magnificent works of King Simandius, narrated thus far from **Diodorus** <note>Diodorus Siculus, a Greek historian of the 1st century BCE.</note>, clearly declare by their material and their form the purpose and intention for which they were established, regardless of how other historians might interpret them. It is hardly likely that the king would have inscribed on his monument the total sum of gold and silver received annually from the mines as if this wealth were perpetual and his own property, especially since it is always liable to decrease; wealth gathered from mines is rarely stable or consistent, but usually changes suddenly. Furthermore, **Simandius** could not claim these works as his own if he were not the author but merely the steward of them, since that glory would belong equally to his ancestors and his successors. It would seem to border on folly to take care to carve the riches dug from the earth upon one's own tomb after death. Moreover, the sum is so great <margin>1,320,000,000 Crowns.</margin> that it is incredible if it is said to be the annual yield from the mines, as it far exceeds a thousand million pieces of gold. 

Therefore, I would say that there is something mystical hidden beneath this, or perhaps a finite number was used to represent an infinite one. For this inscription is followed by the **Sacred Library**—that is, a collection of sacred books or those written in **hieroglyphic letters**—bearing the title, **Medicine for the Soul** <note>original: "Animi medicamentum"</note>. What else does this indicate than what is said by **Solomon** in *Wisdom*, chapter 7 (as quoted in the *Rosary of the Philosophers* <note>A famous 16th-century alchemical text that blends spiritual wisdom with chemical philosophy.</note>): *In comparison to it [Wisdom], all gold is like a little sand, and silver will be valued as clay in its sight. For its acquisition is better than the trading of silver and the purest gold. Its fruit is more precious than all the riches of this world, and everything desired in the world cannot be compared to it.*

After it has been nourished and worshipped for four years in the temple of <term>Vulcan</term> <note>The Roman name for the Egyptian god Ptah, the patron of Memphis and a god of fire and craftsmanship.</note>, it is submerged alive into a certain spring with great solemnity; its corpse is carried to a most sumptuous Tomb, and afterwards it is called **Serapis**. Then another bull, marked with the same spots and colors as before, is sought with great care by the Priests throughout the entire region of Egypt. How most sumptuous palaces, called *Bedchambers* <note>original: "Cubilia"</note>, were built for this bull by the Memphites in the temple of Vulcan, with what anxiety they cared for and nourished it, and with what reverence and worship they followed it, can be noted scattered among various Authors:

<margin>
How long the Apis was worshipped by the Egyptians.
</margin>
*Diodorus* testifies that this custom of worshipping the bull lasted into his own time, having been observed for many centuries before then. If we consider the idolatry of the Israelite people, led out of Egypt by *Moses*, which was instituted in the desert by Aaron’s permission—how they made a calf out of gold and paid divine honors to it by dancing around it in the Egyptian rite—we will realize that the worship of Apis was received in Egypt long before that time. For *Moses* led the Israelite people out of Egypt around the year of the world 2454 (before the birth of Christ, 1509); and *Diodorus Siculus* traveled through Egypt in the year of the world 3907 (before the birth of Christ, 55). From this calculation, it is clear that the interval between the exodus of *Moses* and the pilgrimage of *Diodorus* is 1453 years, during which time the rite of worshipping the bull in Egypt remained continuous, both long before and after. The Egyptians themselves are ignorant of the true causes of this institution, as it is most ancient, and therefore they publicly propose the most diverse reasons. For thus says *Diodorus* in the said second book: "The honor bestowed upon the bull..."

# Book 1 of the Egypto-Greeks

Others say that after Osiris was killed by **Typhon** <note>The Greek name for the Egyptian god Set, the brother and rival of Osiris</note>, Apis gathered his limbs and placed them in a wooden cow covered with white cowhide; for this reason, the city was named **Busiris** <note>From the Egyptian "Pr-Wsir," meaning the House of Osiris</note>. They tell many other fables about Apis, which would take long to relate individually. However, the Egyptians, by discussing all these wondrous and incredible honors for such animals, have cast no small doubt on those seeking the true causes.

<margin>Deeper secrets.</margin>
The Priests possess certain secret writings, as we have already said. Many of the Egyptians give three reasons, the first of which is entirely fabulous and worthy of the simplicity of the ancients.

<margin>The First Cause.</margin>
For they say that the earlier Gods, when they were few in number and unequal in strength to the people, and fearing the impiety of men, disguised themselves as certain animals, and in that way escaped the cruelty and violence of men. 

<margin>Fables of worshipped animals.</margin>
Later, having gained dominion over the world, to return favor to the animals that had provided the cause of their safety, they consecrated those whose form they had taken, and showed how they should be nourished while living and buried when dead.

<margin>The Second Cause.</margin>
They relate that the ancient Egyptians, among whom there was no military doctrine, were often conquered in war by their neighbors. They devised the idea of carrying a certain <term>standard</term> <note>original: "insigne," a military emblem or banner used to organize troops</note> that the soldiers might follow. Therefore, their leaders carried figures of the animals they now worship into war; because of this, by recognizing and maintaining the order under which each soldier fought, they achieved victory. Thus, it seemed right to return favor to these animals as the authors of victory, and it was decreed a sin to kill any of those whose image had been carried, but rather they should be worshipped and treated with honor.

<margin>The Third Cause.</margin>
A third cause is brought forward: the usefulness of these animals for human sustenance. The female cow gives birth to others that plow the earth, and she herself is not useless for plowing. Sheep give birth twice <note>original: "bis edunt fetus," referring to their high fertility</note> and provide wool suited for various uses, as well as an abundance of milk and cheese for us. The dog is useful both for hunting and for guarding. Therefore, the god who is called **Anubis** <note>The jackal-headed god associated with mummification and the afterlife</note> among them, with the head...

# Book 1. Of the Egyptian-Greeks.

[Dio]dorus <note>original: "dorus", the conclusion of "Diodorus"</note> confesses that certain more secret writings about these matters exist among the Priests, as yet unknown to others. The nature of these secrets—such that they could and were accustomed to be called a **Medicine for the Soul**—has been revealed by later times. Therefore, let those three causes <note>The three historical explanations previously discussed: military signals, utility, and gratitude</note>—fit to be mocked by children and discordant with all truth—be gone; let whoever will believe them. For us, other reasons have become known. If, however, those same stories were spoken as Allegory, they can stand together; the first part, which is most absurd according to the letter, will correspond more closely to the truth in its underlying sense.

For since the alchemical gods <note>original: "dij chymici"</note>, **Osiris**, **Isis**, **Mercury**, and **Vulcan**, feared the impiety of men, they did not wish to bestow their works upon them without discrimination. Therefore, under the figure and form of various living creatures, they veiled and hid them as if with a skin, so that they might not be recognized except by those initiated <note>original: "conscijs"</note> or by the rational. It was not safe to openly entrust the most secret mysteries of nature to Nilotic papyrus <note>Paper made from the papyrus plant of the Nile</note> or animal skins <note>parchment</note> in plain writing; rather, it seemed advisable to communicate with one another using essential characters taken from living creatures, so that those listening or watching would not know, but those who already knew would not be ignorant.

To make this more evident, we shall briefly examine the reason for this divine worship paid to the ox, called **Apis**, from which a similar judgment must be made regarding the others.

## Book I of the Hieroglyphics

...by plowing, harrowing, threshing, and other most laborious tasks, he <note>the ox</note> applies himself to this work. This is both because he vividly represents the image of the crescent moon through his horns and the white spots upon his black body, and because he is varied in color, gentle by nature, and not at all difficult to find. While others may observe different properties, these are sufficient for our purpose. Moreover, this ox is a visible and tangible image of *Isis* and *Osiris*, serving as a bridge for the intelligent observer to return to the higher meaning—that is, what is actually signified by it. But here one might ask: was the establishment of such a cult so necessary that the <term>chymical</term> <note>original: "chymicum"; referring to the art of alchemy, which the author believes was the secret science of the Egyptians</note> art could not be practiced without it?

<margin>Two primary motives for worshipping the ox. 1.</margin>
To this I reply that there are two primary motives or driving causes for the introduction of these ceremonies and rituals. The first and most important was so that daily thanks might be offered to God—the supreme Creator and Giver of such great gifts—by the initiated priests. Upon seeing this animal, they viewed it as a visible object and a kind of outward sacrament and symbol, reminding them to direct the inner movements of their hearts toward God. Furthermore, it served so that younger priests—who had not yet attained a perfect knowledge of this matter—might be encouraged by these <term>hieroglyphic</term> <note>original: "hieroglyphicis"; sacred symbolic carvings used to hide and reveal philosophical truths</note> characters to investigate things that were more obscure. For it is believable that the disciples of the philosophers trained one another in these fundamentals by examining and contemplating the images or figures of things and animals. Their goal was to become perfect theorists before setting their hands to practice. Just as the mind more easily retains what the hand has previously noted, so the hand more aptly expresses what the mind has thoroughly prepared in advance.

<margin>2. The second cause.</margin>
The second and secondary cause concerns the common people. First, it was to keep them (though ignorant of the deeper meaning) occupied with the duty and veneration of this animal, ensuring they remained compliant with the laws. Second, it was to prevent them from prying into the deeds and writings of the Sages who practiced the art of <term>Chymia</term> <note>Alchemy</note>. For if no external worship had been attached to this matter, those Priests would not have been called Priests at all, but rather <term>chymical</term> artisans. Out of curiosity, everyone would have pried into their actions and results...

It is also clear that the philosophical matter <term>philosophical matter</term> <note>original: "materiam philosophicam"; the raw substance or "First Matter" used by alchemists to begin the Great Work</note> is denoted by the bull. Moreover, in later times, the Greeks always allegorically suggested this same matter through cattle. This is seen in the Bull of Minos (or the Minotaur) enclosed in the Cretan labyrinth and defeated by Theseus with the help of Ariadne; in the cattle of Hercules driven away from Hesperia or Iberia <note>ancient names for the Spanish peninsula</note> from the three-bodied Geryon (the son of Chrysaor and grandson of Medusa’s blood), namely from the Pyrenean mountains; in the cattle of the Sun pastured in Trinacria <note>an ancient name for Sicily</note>; in the bulls brought under the yoke by Jason; and in many other such examples.

The color of this Apis bull had to be black for the same reason: because "blacker than black" <note>original: "nigrum nigrius nigro"; a standard alchemical phrase describing the *nigredo* or "blackness," the first stage of the chemical process involving decay and transformation</note> is the beginning of the Art. Moreover, a white spot in the shape of a crescent moon was required on its forehead or one of its sides; otherwise, it was required to be a young bull or calf, healthy and noble, entirely without other spots. This is because a younger age is required, just as in eggs suitable for hatching, so too in the philosophical matter. And just as a hen's eggs produced without a rooster are useless, so the philosophical subject, or Apis, is of little use without the image of the crescent moon.

Apis does not exceed his fourth year; when that time arrives, he is drowned, and another is sought in his place, and in the same way is nourished, worshipped, and extinguished. This is because it is necessary for him to remain young. For once the course of *Philosophy* <note>the alchemical process or cycle</note> has been completed three or four times, it is begun anew, so that Typhon might again slay Osiris, and Isis might gather the limbs of her husband once more. Others say that Isis is the moon and Osiris is the sun—the celestial ones—and that Apis is sacred to them, especially being marked with the said spots. This is the origin and root of the animalistic superstition of the Egyptians in worshipping all kinds of animals and plants, arising from Apis and his hieroglyphics, sown and fixed in their minds; for while the commoner took the sign for the thing signified out of ignorance—just as a dog, out of anger, snaps at a stone instead of the thrower—and clung to the external surface, he neglected the inner things which were meant to be perceived by the intellect, not the eyes; and while he chased the shadow, he lost the essence of the thing. Thus superstition was born from superstition and error from error, with the Priests turning a blind eye to this for the reasons mentioned before; nor indeed could such an opinion, drunk in with their mother's milk, be later rooted out, unless the truth were revealed—the truth of why such great things were ordained by the ancients, which was in no way permitted.

And the author of the German rhythms says: "*Alexander* <note>The alchemical tradition often attributed texts to Alexander the Great</note> writes from Persia that the Wolf and the Dog were raised in this clay; yet the Philosopher indicates to us that both have one origin, namely that the Wolf comes from the East, while the Dog has its origin in the West."

<margin>The Cat.</margin>
In the same way, the Cat was held sacred to Isis for the same reason: because *Isis* was likened to the celestial Moon and to the female nature, and the cat seemed to maintain the fluctuations of the Moon through the increase and decrease of its eyes. For this reason, the cat was held in the highest honor among the superstitious Egyptians, and it was considered a capital crime to have killed a cat. As *Diodorus* <note>Diodorus Siculus, a Greek historian</note> relates, a certain Roman commoner and a Persian King were slaughtered because of injuries inflicted upon a cat.

<margin>The Lion.</margin>
They placed the Lion as the king of animals, which was of a victorious nature, hot and fiery, and which lived on the blood of others; by this, they denoted sulfur marked with a "lion's skin." Since we have spoken of this more frequently in these books, we omit it here as something already well-known.

<margin>The He-goat.</margin>
The He-goat is observed to designate the same things as *Typhon, Priapus, the Phallus, Satyrs, and Titans*. For since it is an animal prone to lust, as is clear from *Virgil’s Eclogues, 3*:

> We know who [watched] you, while the he-goats looked askance,
> and in what shrine—but the easy-going Nymphs just laughed.

*Augustine* <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430)</note> mentions this in *Book 2, chapter 14* of *The City of God*, where *Thomas Valois* <note>Thomas Waleys (c. 1270–1350), a Dominican theologian known for commenting on Augustine</note> adds that *Augustine* understands the *Dog-headed Baboon* to be *Mercury or the Egyptian Hermes*; hence he also says in *Book 2, chapters 12 and 16*: "I truly wonder if she herself, namely *Rhea*, the mother of the Gods, gave birth to the *Dog-head*, who came much later from *Egypt*." *Isidore*, in *Book 8, final chapter*, says that this *Mercury or Hermes* was formed with a dog's head; for the Dog is a most keen-witted animal, and thus Hermes himself was the wisest. These are the words of *Valois*.

Very similar to this animal (if it is not the same) is the one called the *Baboon* <note>original: *Bavian*</note>, whose gestures, like those of an ape, are varied and whose training is marvelous. The reason for this is clear from what was said before, to which others add that by its repeated urination it expresses the twenty-four hours of a natural day, and thus represents the movement of the sun in a circle.

<margin>The Ibis.</margin>
The same reasoning applies to the Ibis, which was considered extremely beneficial to Egypt for preying upon serpents. This bird was believed to be sacred to *Isis* and *Mercury* <note>original: *Mercurio*; the author identifies the Roman Mercury with the Egyptian Thoth</note> because of secret natural gifts: both because it made the air healthier and life safer for animals by devouring venomous things, and because it cured itself of obstructions that blocked its bowels by injecting itself with a clyster <note>original: *Clysteris*; an ancient term for an enema. <margin>The Hawk.</margin>
They consider the Hawk sacred to *Osiris*, because it is seen as a solar bird, not only on account of the sharpness of its eyes, in which it excels, but also its fiery nature ready for war; hence that line of *Ovid*:

> *We hate the hawk, because it always lives in arms.* <note>original: "Odimus accipitrem, quia semper vivit in armis," from Ovid's *Ars Amatoria*</note>

Indeed, by this martial force it calls other birds to be its prey and converts them into its own blood.

<margin>The Eagle.</margin>
Above all these, however, they recognized the Eagle as the Queen of birds, and placed it among the sacred characters which the Egyptians call Hieroglyphics, for the same reasons we have reviewed before, and will review later where the Eagle is mentioned. Besides these Hieroglyphic figures, countless others are found, such as on the Pyramids, the Table of Isis <note>original: *Isidis mensa*; referring to the Bembine Tablet, a famous bronze tablet of Egyptian-style imagery that fascinated Renaissance scholars</note>, and similar ancient Egyptian works.

# Book 1 of the Hieroglyphics.

<margin>Glass in Egypt from ancient times.</margin>
Glass, which could be called an <term>artificial stone</term> <note>original: "lapis artificialis"</note> that is transparent and properly belongs to the study of <term>chemistry</term> <note>original: "chymiam"; in this context, it refers to the alchemical and chemical arts of transforming materials</note>, was known from the most ancient times in Egypt and neighboring Ethiopia. By this method, when placed in elevated spots, a golden image resembling the deceased is presented to the viewers through the surrounding glass. And they affirm these to be the tombs of the wealthy; the less well-off use silver images, while the poor use clay ones. Since glass is produced in great abundance in Ethiopia, everyone possesses it. We thought these things should be brought forward because the Ethiopians once ruled the Egyptians, and the Egyptians ruled a great part of the Ethiopians; this is so that no one might conclude otherwise than the truth—perhaps thinking there was a lack of the vessels now required for the use of <term>chemistry</term> <note>original: "chymiæ"</note> at that time—but rather see the reality of the situation.

# Book 1 of the Hieroglyphics

...judgment, some will declare all things vain, useless, and consistent with neither reason nor nature. They do this because they themselves do not grasp or understand the method of perfecting—according to art—those works which are of nature. Nor do they see artisans of this kind openly performing such great and significant works; instead, they only see the common practitioners, who are more famous for fraud and poverty than for true artistry and wealth. To these and similar objections—which conclude negatively and depend on what they call an "ignorance of the law and the fact" <note>original: "ignorantia juris et facti"; a legal principle used here to suggest critics neither understand the rules of alchemy nor the historical evidence of its success</note>—we respond as follows: 

(Since with such objections one might, with the same ease and audacity, overturn celestial things as well as terrestrial ones, despite the many experiments existing on both sides to the contrary.) 

The facts already stated sufficiently prove that the Egyptians, and their followers among the most ancient Greeks, possessed a **Golden Medicine**. They used this not only to sustain the health of the body but also for the acquisition of riches. This has been handed down in the records of ancient historians since the time of *Diocletian* <note>The Roman Emperor Diocletian (r. 284–305 AD) famously ordered the burning of Egyptian books on alchemy to prevent them from financing rebellions</note>. 

Truly, this was not the primary aim of my proposition—or perhaps only a secondary one—which would sufficiently prove itself if only the Medicine I primarily undertook to demonstrate were established. For many and various powers, efficacies, virtues, goals, and effects can belong to a **single Subject**, even if they are not all directed toward one and the same intention. 

This is clearly seen in **gold**, that most noble subject: 
- Physicians use it to cure human health.
- Craftsmen use it to fashion other works.
- Others use it for ornament and display.
- Not a few use it for profit and wealth. 

(For what does gold not accomplish?) 

So it is also to be thought regarding that **gold-begotten Medicine** <note>original: "Medicina aurigena"; refers to the alchemical Elixir or Philosopher's Stone, believed to be "born" from gold or capable of producing it</note>. We do not deny that many Egyptian kings abused it for luxury and riches, as well as for introducing Idolatry and confirming it under the silence of the most secret mysteries. However, many others also used it for divine glory, for the benefit of their neighbor, and for preserving the health of the human body. Since a name should be given based on the superior part <note>A philosophical principle: "a potiori fit denominatio," meaning a thing should be defined by its best or most important quality</note>, and since there is more value in addressing the fragility and brevity of human life, according to the precept...

## ON THE HIEROGLYPHICS OF THE GREEKS, AND

### Firstly, regarding Allegories more CONSPICUOUS than gold.

<margin>
The gods received by all nations, originating from Vulcan and Mercury.

**I**F WE TRACE BACK the beginning and primary origin of the most diverse religions accepted among all nations at any time, we will find that they have always arisen from probable causes. We embrace the most ancient religion of the Old Testament—held by the Fathers before the flood, and afterwards propagated from the age of Abraham to the Israelites—as the truest of all, setting it apart from all others, inasmuch as it was instituted by God himself and demonstrated by innumerable miracles. To this succeeded the Christian profession of the NEW TESTAMENT, a calling greater than any exception. We speak here especially of the Idolatry of the heathens, or the veneration and worship of false deities. Without doubt, this was occasioned by causes that appeared to be not entirely fabricated or believed to be false, but rather reasonable, plausible, and established by the consensus of many. Thus almost the entire world (excepting the Jewish Commonwealth <term>Polytia</term> <note>From the Greek 'politeia', referring here to the unique civil and religious governance of the Jewish people under divine law.</note>) drew its deities from the Romans by whom they were ruled; the Romans from the Greeks; the Greeks from the Egyptians; the common people of the Egyptians from the Priests; and the priests from Vulcan and Mercury, Osiris and Isis—their deities existing as fictions and "golden" ones <note>The author implies these "golden" gods are allegories for alchemical secrets or the "Great Work."</note>, or at the very least, as names [the matter...]

# Book 2. Of the Egyptian-Greeks.

...signifying an entirely different matter, they borrowed the whole use and rite of sacrifices; concerning which we have thus far discussed clearly enough under the Egyptian Hieroglyphics.

<margin>The twelve Egyptian Gods called the gods of the great nations.</margin>
Besides the aforementioned *Osiris, Isis, and Horus*, the most ancient Egyptians also made use of the names of other Gods, especially twelve: namely *Jupiter, Neptune, Mars, Mercury, Vulcan, Apollo, Juno, Vesta, Ceres, Venus, Diana, and Minerva*. Six of these are of the Masculine and as many of the feminine sex; and these were believed to be the great Gods of the great nations, and were later transferred to the Greeks, and from them to the Romans. For as *Natalis* <note>Natalis Comes (1520–1582), a famous Renaissance mythographer whose work "Mythologiae" was a standard reference for interpreting ancient fables.</note> testifies, for others, images were made of wood or clay, and they were not sculpted from gold, silver, or ivory—except for the great Gods—whereas the Plebeian <note>Lower-ranking or "common" deities.</note> gods were made of any material in ancient times. Concerning these, *Herodotus* says in *Euterpe* <note>The second book of Herodotus's 'Histories,' which focuses on Egypt.</note>: *The Egyptians were the first to believe in the names of the twelve Gods, and that the Greeks took them from them; and they were the first to erect altars and images and Temples to the Gods for themselves.*

<margin>The Greeks received teachings from the Egyptians.</margin>
But as to how the Greeks—and which among them were the first—traveled to the Egyptians and brought their sacred rites back into Greece, we shall demonstrate by the words of *Diodorus* himself. Here in Book 2, Chapter 6 <note>Referring to 'Bibliotheca historica' by Diodorus Siculus.</note>, he says: "Now we shall recount which **Greeks endowed with wisdom and learning traveled to Egypt in ancient times** so that they might perceive their laws and doctrine."

<margin>Which Greeks first traveled into Egypt.</margin>
Their priests write that it is contained in the sacred books that there first traveled to the Egyptians *Orpheus, Musaeus, Melampus, Daedalus, Homer* the Poet, and *Lycurgus* of Sparta; next *Solon* of Athens, *Plato* the Philosopher, and *Pythagoras* of Samos; also *Eudoxus* the Mathematician, and *Democritus* of Abdera, and *Oenopides* of Chios. Traces of all of them are shown: images of some, and locations of others, named either after them or from the doctrine which they followed. In Egypt they certainly perceived everything that made them admirable among the Greeks. For they report that *Orpheus* brought back most of the hymns of the Gods, the mysteries <term>orgia</term> <note>The word 'orgia' here refers to secret religious rites or "mysteries," particularly those of Dionysus, rather than the modern sense of the word.</note>, and the fiction of the underworld; indeed, the ceremonies of *Osiris* and *Dionysus* are the same, and the names of *Isis* and *Ceres* are similar...

When the Egyptian sacred rites were transferred to the Greeks.

Six primary authors of fabulous religion among the Greeks.

### Book 2. Of the Egyptian-Greeks. 59

<margin>The primary intention of the most ancient poets.</margin>

...slaughtering a triumphant victor; but if we wish to inquire more deeply into the intention of **Orpheus** <note>A legendary musician and prophet in Greek myth, whom the author treats as a real historical figure who brought Egyptian wisdom to Greece.</note> and other ancient poets, we will find in truth that they did not look primarily toward those divine cults or ceremonies, but toward other most secret matters <term>arcanissima</term> <note>Most secret or hidden things; in this context, it often refers to alchemical or natural secrets.</note> hidden beneath them. This was done so that these secrets would not become known to the common people, yet would provide the wiser sort with a reason for investigation. Although this has been indicated by no other writer (because the matter remained hidden and was not even expressed by name), it can nevertheless be most clearly shown by us from various clues and arguments gathered here and there, as will appear in the following pages. 

Even if these were not considered, this single reason would suffice for those with understanding: namely, if the **Egyptians** intended something other by their sacred rites and ceremonies involving **Osiris**, **Isis**, **Mercury**, **Vulcan**, **Apis**, and certain animals, than the objects visible to the eyes, and hid a kernel of truth under them as if under husks; likewise, the **Greeks** would not have been concerned with the coverings unless they also recognized a "body" to be covered beneath them. 

What sort of "body" <note>The "body" refers to the core physical or philosophical truth being dressed up in mythological stories.</note> that was, we have already sufficiently investigated and explained above under the **Egyptian Hieroglyphics**. Hence, it is not likely that those ancient poets—out of innate malice or for the sake of mockery—attributed so many adulteries, homicides, incests, and crimes to their Gods to trick either gods or men, or to propagate such enormous vices by the examples of the Gods (for then they would have been the most wicked of all two-legged creatures). Rather, they did this to demonstrate that those Gods were nothing but fictitious, imaginary symbols and **Emblems** of a secret art <term>artis occultae</term>—well known to themselves though hidden from the common people—referring to one thing for the eye, and another for the mind. 

Lest they should seem to bring forward empty names devoid of reality, they assigned to each of those fictitious Gods individual, seemingly divine duties and various powers of mother **Nature**, yet they nonetheless professed **one God** <note>original: "Vnum Deum"</note> in all of them. This appears more clearly in the most ancient writers than in others. For in this way, **Orpheus** interprets the individual Gods according to common understanding, and then adds that all things are one...

1. The Allegory of the Golden Fleece of Jason. Orpheus was the first of the Greek poets, theologians, and lawgivers.

Just as **Orpheus** was the author of religion among the Greeks, so too did he stand out as the first inventor and herald of the allegory concerning the seeking of the **Golden Fleece** from **Colchis**. He devised this with singular subtlety and perfected it with skill, with precisely the same intention and end for which many writings of a more recent age have been published on a similar subject; namely, that there might be a double sense: the superficial and the hidden. 

The superficial sense follows the letter and is historical, or if it does not follow the letter entirely, it nevertheless explains common and ordinary matters concerning morals or the nature of things. The hidden sense, however, looks toward the internal essence; it suggests secrets removed from the common people's knowledge to the wise, while hiding them from those of lesser intellect. 

This author also wrote other works in verse, which he himself recounts in the *Argonautica* <note>The epic poem telling the story of Jason and the Argonauts' quest for the Golden Fleece.</note>, proving the supreme sharpness of his talent and learning. Among these, in his book on precious stones, he vividly depicts the **Cave of Mercury** from which all kinds of good things are to be brought back. He does this so clearly that whoever has a "sharp nose" <note>original: "emunctae naris"; a Latin idiom for someone with keen discernment or wit.</note>, and is not blocked by phlegm <note>original: "pituita." In ancient medicine, an excess of phlegm was thought to make a person dull-witted or sluggish.</note>, may easily catch the scent of what he intends by the Cave of Mercury there, and what subject he wishes to be understood in the *Argonautica*. But we shall first run through the sequence of his narrative, and then add our own notes on the other side, along with the concordances of nature and other authors.

**Pelias**, the son of **Neptune** born from **Tyro** (the daughter of **Salmoneus** who was raised by Salmoneus's brother **Cretheus**), would have obtained **Iolcus** after the death of Cretheus, who had founded the city. Therefore, so that Pelias might expose Jason to present dangers and even to death itself under an honorable pretext, he gave him orders to bring back to him the famous **Golden Fleece** <note>original: "Vellus aureum"</note> from **Colchis**, overcoming all perils with the singular fortitude of spirit that befitted such a young man. Although this seemed difficult to command and arduous to perform, it nevertheless gave courage to Jason, because it fell to him to carry it out not from his own insolence, but by the command of another, whom it would be a sin to disobey. 

Therefore, having prepared the necessities for the journey with fifty companions—nearly all of whom traced their descent from the gods—he boarded the ship, the ***Argo***, which had been built by the advice of **Pallas** <note>Athena</note> and featured a talking mast <note>original: "malum loquacem"</note> made from a **Dodonian oak**. ...which some have called the clashing rocks <note>These are the Symplegades, legendary islands at the mouth of the Bosphorus that supposedly crushed ships passing between them.</note>, from which a great deal of fire gushed forth. They explored the danger of these rocks by first releasing a dove. From there, leaving Bithynia far off to the side, they sailed past the island of Thynias, the lands of the Mariandyni, Acherusia, the city of the Eneti, Carambis, the rivers Halys and Iris, Themiscyra, Cappadocia, the land of the Chalybes, and countless other places. They eventually reached the river Phasis, which flows through the land of Circe, and finally arrived at the **Golden Fleece**. 

When Jason and his companions were led to **Aeetes**, the son of the Sun and King of the Colchians, they were generously received by him. In response to Jason's requests, the King replied that he would grant him the Golden Fleece—which was placed in the midst of all as a prize—only if he could obtain it through both "Mars and art" <note>In this context, "Mars" refers to physical strength or warfare, while "art" refers to technical skill or alchemical knowledge.</note>. 

Since the dangers appeared insurmountable, Aeetes’ own daughter, **Medea**, told Jason to be of good heart. At night, she provided him with certain highly proven medicines <term>pharmaca</term>, by the proper administration of which he would escape whatever dangers might exist. Nor did this hope fail him. Now, the Golden Fleece was hanging in the **Grove of Mars**, inside a garden surrounded by very strong walls; in its vestibule stood most ferocious bulls with feet of brass <term>æripedes</term> and a dragon with very long teeth who served as ever-watchful guardians. 

<margin>The law established for the one who would take the Golden Fleece.</margin>
The law governing the challenge was set as follows: first, the dragon had to be killed and its teeth knocked out of its head; then, the bulls were to be brought under the yoke and the earth split with a plow; the teeth were then to be scattered into the soil, and the sudden crop of armed men that would spring up from them had to be cut down. Once these tasks were completed, the Golden Fleece would be granted to the victor; if not, the defeated man must face death. 

<margin>Four medicines given to Jason by Medea.</margin>
Medea, however, had given Jason four specific medicines:
1.  **First**, an ointment with which he was to rub his body, so that he might escape unharmed from the poison and fire of the dragon and the bulls.
2.  **Second**, a certain sleep-inducing mass which, if he threw it into the jaws of the dragon, would cause the beast to fall instantly into a deep sleep.
3.  **Third**, a certain clear water that would most easily extinguish the fire of the bulls.
4.  **Fourth**, an image of the **Moon** and the **Sun** crafted in a peculiar way; if he wore this around his neck, whatever he attempted in this work would succeed perfectly.

With these things properly prepared...

<margin>Jason’s battle.</margin>
...having put it to use, on the following day he began the battle. But when Jason had anointed himself with the aforementioned ointment and fortified himself with that image hanging from his neck <note>This likely refers to a protective talisman or amulet Medea provided Jason to shield him from the dragon's breath.</note>, he threw that narcotic mass <term>narcoticam</term> into its open mouth.
